Definition: as abstractly (in plural masculine) a ransom
BiblicalUsage: Pâdûwy is the ransom money, counted in shekels, paid for the firstborn of Israel beyond the number of the Levites. Moses takes the redemption money from those who are to be redeemed and gives it to Aaron and his sons.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that this small accounting in Numbers teaches a large truth: every firstborn belongs to God, and redemption is always reckoned and paid, never assumed.
